cases.why: INCIDENT 2026-07-29 (85 PDFs found, ZERO moved, reported 'Done — 2 step(s) completed') plus INCIDENT 2026-07-30 (the fix moved 85 including 8 out of a source repo, because the mutation guards still keyed on the singular tool name). Twelve top-level files exceed BATCH_EXPAND_MAX=8, so this exercises the move_files batch path — the shape rule 4 now tells the planner to draft — and the nested pair pins the top-level-only default. FOUND AS A GAP BY THIS BENCH 2026-08-03 (reproduced 5/5 runs: all 14 moved) and FIXED the same day. ROOT CAUSE: the scope rules lived inside placeholder_resolver._file_pool, which only resolve() calls — i.e. only while the step still carries a 'PENDING:' placeholder — so a revise/refine round that wrote the CONCRETE list skipped the partition, the truncated-source refusal AND the 'excluded N nested files' note. Third instance of one defect class (2026-07-30 keyed on the singular tool names; 2026-08-01 _DIR_KEY covered reads but not writes). The rules now take a POOL rather than a step (placeholder_resolver.mutation_scope) and BOTH entry points are thin callers; planner._execute_node consults scope_concrete_list on every pass, before the approval gate.

cases.why: The pre-flight path guard: a WRITE/DESTRUCTIVE step whose target provably does not exist fails into the replan loop BEFORE the approval pause — the user is never asked to approve a guessed path. ⚠️ THIS CASE FIRST ASSERTED status_any=[failed, awaiting_choice] AND THAT EXPECTATION WAS WRONG: the plan legitimately ends COMPLETED with 'No matching files were found … nothing to do', which is placeholder_resolver's documented behaviour ('an outcome, not a failure'). Corrected to pin what actually matters — no delete tool ever ran, no approval was ever requested for a guessed path, and the user was told plainly that nothing was found. A test that asserts an incidental status instead of the guarantee is a test that reports a defect where there is none. NOTE: this case is legitimately VARIABLE — the planner sometimes completes with that message and sometimes pauses to ask 'where is it?' (the documented ask-not-fail recovery). Both are correct, and the harness reports the second as BLOCKED rather than failing it.

cases.why:
THE MEASUREMENT FOR ITEM 6. `notes` is a DIRECTORY, so run 1 dead-ends on read_file ('path is a directory, not a file') and the plan gives up. That run now writes a plan_traces row naming the tool, the reason and the fail class. Run 2 asks the IDENTICAL goal against the SAME sandbox and the SAME database, so the RECENT FAILURES block is available to the planner, and rule 23's own worked example is exactly this case (read_file failed because the path is a directory -> list_directory instead).

TWO NUMBERS, NOT ONE. `retry_signal_present` asks whether the mechanism ENGAGED (was the record there and readable?); `retry_avoids_tools` asks whether it CHANGED ANYTHING. Conflating those is how the 2026-07-17 fan-out shipped a feature that never fired while 1,578 tests stayed green.

⚠️ THE SECOND NUMBER IS ALLOWED TO BE ZERO, and if it is, the recorded instruction is NOT to rewrite the prompt — this codebase has measured prompt-only rules at zero three separate times. Either find a comparator or delete the block. See the honest limit in app/core/failure_intelligence.py.
